chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْه، عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينَ، عَنِ الْمَدَائِنِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامِ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Ya'qub, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali b. Yaqtin, from al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي: يَا مُرَازِمُ مَنْ بَشَّارٌ؟ قُلْتُ: بَيَّاعُ الشَّعِيرِ، قَالَ: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ بَشَّارًا، قَالَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ لِي: يَا مُرَازِمُ قُلْ لَهُمْ وَيْلَكُمْ تُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ فَإِنَّكُمْ كَافِرُونَ مُشْرِكُونَ

translations.en: He said to me: O Murazim – who is Bashshar? I said: the seller of barley, he said: may Allah curse Bashshar, then he said to me: O Murazim – say to them: woe on you! repent to Allah for you are indeed disbelieving polytheists!

en.summary: In this narration from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the barley seller Bashshar as a representative of the Khawarij or early sectarians who deviated from the Ahl al-Bayt, cursing him for his specific brand of takfir. The Imam then commands Murazim to convey the Quranic verse 'you are disbelieving polytheists' (Kafarum Mushrikun), linking Bashshar’s group to the broader Quranic critique of those who claim monotheism but engage in idolatrous practices of their own making. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that the Khawarij’s excommunication of others constituted a form of shirk due to their rigid, error-prone judgment.
en.seo_question: Who is Bashshar and why did Imam al-Sadiq curse him in this hadith?
